rationale:
Obligations from `requirements.sdk.graph.search.occurrence`: (1) one result per occurrence, including several on one line or in one item; (2) each hit carries the enclosing node, the exact matched text and a file-relative span (zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets, end exclusive); (3) both `SourceProject::search_text` and `SourceProject::search_structure` return these hits; (4) the `SearchHit` shape, with public `node`, `span` and `text`, plus `new` and `Debug`.

Coverage in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs`:
- `mod[tests]/fn[search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration]` covers `search_text`. The source is `const A = "éhit"; const B = "hit hit";` on a single line. It asserts exactly three hits as (node, span, text) tuples:
  - `const[A]` at 19..22 with text "hit".
  - `const[B]` at 42..45 and again at 46..49.
  - This covers one result per occurrence, two hits in one item, and several hits on one line. The 2-byte `é` shifts the offsets, so byte offsets (not chars) and the 0-based, end-exclusive convention are checked. The enclosing node and the exact text are asserted.
- `mod[tests]/fn[structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item]` covers `search_structure`. It uses `fn one(){call();} fn two(){call();}` on one line. It asserts hits `code.rs#fn[one]` 9..15 "call()" and `code.rs#fn[two]` 27..33 "call()". It also asserts that the spans equal `StructuralRule::matches` on the file text. This covers the structural entry point with correct node, text and span, and two same-line occurrences in different items.
- The tests read `h.node`, `h.span` and `h.text` directly, so the public fields are exercised.

Remaining points:
- `SearchHit::new` returns `Result`, but the requirement text names no failure behavior for it. An untested invalid-span path is therefore not a named boundary.
- The `Debug` implementation is a derive with no conditional or transformation of its own, so it needs no test.
- Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.

text: Return one result per occurrence, including multiple matches on the same line or in the same item. Each result contains the enclosing `NodeId<D>`, the exact matched text, and its file-relative `Span` in the retained UTF-8 source (zero-based byte offsets, end exclusive). `SourceProject::search_text` and `SourceProject::search_structure` return these hits. Rust callers can use the node ID to load the item's contents and choose their own presentation.
